Background

Ocasio-Cortez has represented parts of the Bronx and Queens since 2019. She toured the country with Sen. Bernie Sanders in 2025 and has become one of the best-known progressives in the party.

Outlook

She has said she would decide after the midterms between a presidential run and a Senate challenge to Chuck Schumer, and she has not yet announced a choice. Prediction markets rate her second, near 15 percent, and the New York City chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America voted on November 14 to urge her to run. A Senate run would be a lower-risk path, which holds her odds below the top tier.

Recent Headlines

  • The New York City chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America voted 291 to 123 to encourage her to run for president, though a sizable minority dissented. National Security Journal, Nov 16, 2026
  • In a pre-midterm CNN/SSRS poll, 27 percent of Democrats said they would be excited to support her, tied with Harris for the most. CNN, Nov 11, 2026
  • The Intercept reported that progressives see no obvious alternative to her for a left-wing run, while some strategists say a Senate bid would be easier. The Intercept, Nov 6, 2026
